permit.applies: the worker, on a job offer (paper application to the Directorate of Immigration, which forwards the work permit application to the Directorate of Labour)
permit.first: a job offer on the Icelandic labour market (for a shortage-of-labour permit, the Directorate of Labour's check that no worker is available)

fees.what: application fee, residence permit based on work

permit.union: The Directorate of Labour asks the relevant union (or national federation) for its opinion on a temporary work permit (Act 97/2002 art. 7(1)(b)); the opinion doesn't bind the Directorate, and a negative one must give its reasons (Regulation 339/2005 art. 9).

sources.title: Ísland.is (Directorate of Immigration), Residence permit based on work
sources.said: Residence permits based on work are for individuals that want to reside in Iceland because they have received a job offer on the Icelandic labour market. You can apply for a residence permits based on work For work requiring expert knowledge Due to a shortage of labour For athletes On the basis of a collaboration or service contract … Processing fee The fee for an application is 80.000 ISK . It is no longer possible to pay a service fee for expedited processing.

sources.title: Ísland.is (Directorate of Immigration), Short-term residence permit, rights and obligations
sources.said: The following foreign nationals are exempt from the requirement to obtain a work permit for employment in Iceland for up to 90 days per calendar year: … Artists, with the exception of musicians employed to perform in restaurants.

sources.title: Ísland.is, Reglugerð nr. 339/2005 um atvinnuréttindi útlendinga (as published on Ísland.is, printed 3 August 2026)
sources.said: Atvinnuleyfi sem veitt er í fyrsta skipti skal eigi veitt til lengri tíma en til eins árs en þó aldrei til lengri tíma en sem nemur ráðningartímanum samkvæmt ráðningarsamningi. … Heimilt er að framlengja gildistíma atvinnuleyfis að uppfylltum skilyrðum a–c-liðar 1. mgr. 7. gr. laga um atvinnuréttindi útlendinga um allt að tvö ár í senn … Vinnumálastofnun skal taka ákvörðun um veitingu atvinnuleyfa svo fljótt sem verða má og eigi síðar en tveimur mánuðum eftir að umsókn berst stofnuninni.

Eftirtaldir útlendingar eru undanþegnir kröfu um atvinnuleyfi vegna vinnu í allt að fjórar vikur á ári hér á landi: … b. Listamenn, að undanskildum hljóðfæraleikurum, sem ráða sig til starfa á veitingahúsum. … [9. gr.] Umsögn stéttarfélags skv. b-lið 1. mgr. 7. gr. laganna er ekki bindandi fyrir Vinnumálastofnun við ákvörðun um veitingu atvinnuleyfis. Stéttarfélagið eða landssambandið er veitir umsögn vegna atvinnuleyfis skal jafnframt sérstaklega rökstyðja neikvæða umsögn.

note: Iceland's residence permits based on work (Directorate of Immigration, with the work permit from the Directorate of Labour) come in four kinds: work requiring expert knowledge, shortage of labour, athletes, and a collaboration or service contract; none is named for performers, and which a performer takes isn't stated, so the kind isn't modelled apart. The application fee is 80,000 ISK; expedited processing is no longer sold. Artists (except musicians employed to perform in restaurants) need no work permit for up to 90 days per calendar year, taken as 90 within 365. vinnumalastofnun.is's temporary work permit page returns 404 to this client. Regulation 339/2005 gives the Directorate of Labour (Vinnumálastofnun) the decision, within two months at most; from 8 July 2026 the Directorate of Immigration (Útlendingastofnun) issues temporary work permits, and the regulation as published has not been re-issued for that change. A first permit runs at most a year (never past the contract) and may be extended up to two years at a time. Read 2026-11-04 in Regulation 339/2005 (the version on reglugerd.is, in force from 30 March 2005): the union's opinion. It also exempts artists (other than musicians engaged by restaurants) from the permit for up to four weeks a year (art. 4(b)), which this file's 90 days don't match; later amendments may not be folded into that copy and the Act wasn't readable here, so the exemption wasn't changed here. papers.work.IS settled it the same day: the Act on Foreigners' Right to Work, art. 23, sets 90 days a year (island.is, and the Directorate of Labour's notification form, read 2026-11-04), and the Act outranks the regulation, so the 90 days stand.
